decision.comment:
Preprocessing stage is internally consistent and data-integrity verified. PathMNIST (9-class, 28×28×3, CC BY 4.0) loaded with full official splits (train 89 996 / val 10 004 / test 7 180); archive MD5 a8b06965… matches the recorded value; zero blank or duplicate samples; imbalance ratio 1.63 is modest. Normalization (per-channel z-score from train stats only) is well-justified by the channel statistics (green std 0.177 vs red/blue ~0.124). Augmentations (hflip, brightness, contrast) are built-in primitives and do not require the pending extension approvals; the augmentation factor of 4 yields 359 984 augmented train samples, matching the split manifest. The two pending extension proposals (hflip_pathology_safe, compact_conv_token_transformer) do not invalidate these primitives per pipeline rules.

Warnings carried forward:
1. llm_model_digest is null for qwen3.8 (Ollama) across ingestion, profiling, and the run manifest. Model weights are not checksum-pinned, weakening full reproducibility of any LLM-assisted step. This is a reproducibility gap, not a correctness error, but should be resolved before any downstream LLM-dependent decision is treated as deterministic.
2. The profiling stage returned action=revise / severity=warning, flagging (a) inter-class visual ambiguity at 28×28 resolution (background/debris/mucus, adipose/background, smooth-muscle/stroma) and (b) the requirement that the OOD aggregate be computed as the arithmetic mean of per-severity AUROCs, not a pooled-sample AUROC. Both are methodological reminders for the evaluation stage, not defects in the preprocessing data.
3. The test set (CRC-VAL-HE-7K) originates from a different clinical center; this is correctly flagged in the dataset manifest and split manifest (official_test_separate_center: true). Downstream OOD evaluation must respect the per-severity AUROC averaging rule.
4. Prior-art parameter-budget note: the CCT idea cites 1–4 M parameters while the compact-transformer proposal caps at 3 M. Not contradictory, but downstream specs should reconcile the exact budget.

No deterministic findings are present. All integrity checks (MD5, SHA-256, split sizes, class counts, channel statistics) pass. The preprocessing artefacts are ready for the next stage.

Profiling stage action=revise: downstream evaluation must account for inter-class visual ambiguity at 28×28 resolution (background/debris/mucus, adipose/background, smooth-muscle/stroma)
OOD aggregate must be computed as the arithmetic mean of per-severity AUROCs, not a pooled-sample AUROC; test set is from a different clinical center (CRC-VAL-HE-7K)
Prior-art parameter budget: CCT idea cites 1–4 M vs compact-transformer proposal cap of 3 M; reconcile in downstream specs

Two extension proposals (hflip_pathology_safe, compact_conv_token_transformer) remain pending_review; built-in augmentations in the representation plan are unaffected but the extensions must be resolved before any non-primitive augmentation is applied

request.system: You are an independent software and ML consistency reviewer. Inspect only the supplied evidence. You may raise severity but must never dismiss deterministic findings. No clinical claims. The supplied current UTC timestamp is authoritative. This pipeline uses the standard 28x28 RGB MedMNIST distribution; do not substitute the source-dataset or MedMNIST+ resolution. Only deterministic findings may justify action=stop; unsupported external-memory claims must be warnings requesting verification. ResNet18 has fixed topology; hidden controls base width and depth is ignored. Generic transformer fields are inactive for CNN families and do not make them transformer hybrids. Built-in augmentations (hflip, vflip, rotate90, rotate180, brightness, contrast) do not require extension approval; pending new proposals do not invalidate these primitives. A cited quote establishes traceability, not support for every scientific inference: assess that support separately. The OOD aggregate is the arithmetic mean of the selected score's AUROCs across corruption severities, not a pooled-sample AUROC.
